title: Observability Safety Gates and Export Contract for the Serving Runtime
author: Aisha Malik
body:
Summary

This page defines the observability safety gates and the telemetry export contract for Redwood Inference's serving runtime. It is intended for runtime engineers, SREs, and profiling/observability owners who implement collection pipelines, CI gates, and on-call automation. The document covers: the canonical telemetry schema we export from the runtime, automated safety gate thresholds and actions, sampling/bandwidth budgets, build-time validation, and an operational runbook for escalations.

Goals

- Provide a single source of truth for the telemetry fields the runtime must emit.
- Define deterministic safety gates that prevent regressions in visibility, regressions that could materially affect SLO investigations, or excessive telemetry costs.
- Ensure export formats and tags are stable enough for downstream consumers (dashboards, tracing, billing, ML evals).
- Provide a clear rollout and CI strategy so instrumentation changes are reviewed and verified.

Scope

Applies to:
- All changes to the serving runtime codepath that add/modify telemetry exports (traces, metrics, logs, profile payloads).
- Telemetry export agents (forwarders) shipped with the runtime.
- CI/bench gating that validates telemetry contract.

Out of scope:
- Consumer-side dashboard changes.
- Third-party observability services that only transform data downstream (but contract-breaking transforms are subject to this doc via related_pages).

High-level contract summary

- Every request processed by the runtime must emit: a request-level trace span, a request metrics sample, and a compact request provenance blob when TRACE_SAMPLING=1.
- Telemetry keys and types must match the schema in the "Telemetry Schema" section below.
- Any change to the schema must include: (1) feature flag guarded codepath, (2) CI validation using canonical examples, (3) rollout with shadow-mode 48–72 hours, (4) automated rollback on gate failures.

Telemetry schema (canonical fields)

Below we list the canonical fields and expected types. Downstream consumers rely on these exact keys. Columns: field | type | description | required

- request_id | string | globally unique per logical request | required
- model | string | model identifier (eg: redwood/gptx-7b-v1) | required
- model_variant | string | quantization/precision/variant tag (eg: awq-8, q3f) | optional
- tenant_id | string | customer tenant if present, otherwise "system" | required
- route | string | API route or logical operation (generate, embedding, rerank) | required
- seq_len | integer | request token count or prompt length | required
- tokens_generated | integer | tokens produced by model (post-generation) | optional
- start_timestamp | iso8601 | when request first entered runtime | required
- end_timestamp | iso8601 | when response left runtime | required
- kernel_hint | string | selected kernel identifier (eg: kernel-v2-mma32) | optional
- kvcache_hit_ratio | float | 0.0–1.0 estimate for prefix cache effectiveness | optional
- alloc_bytes | integer | peak additional GPU allocation during request | optional
- error_code | string | runtime/serving error when applicable | optional

Export contract and delivery expectations

1) Formats supported: JSON-lines for metrics/profile blobs; OTLP/HTTP for traces; prometheus-compatible summaries for aggregated series.
2) Field names must be snake_case as above. No field renames without formal change process.
3) Each exported record must include a schema_version field (string) and an event_type tag (trace|metric|profile).

Safety gates (automated checks executed pre- and post-deploy)

We operate two classes of gates: CI-time (build/test) and production-time (runtime monitors + rolling-deploy blockers).

A. CI-time gates (unit/integration tests)
- Telemetry schema compile check: Any change to exported structs must pass jsonschema validation against canonical_examples/*.json.
- Example generation: Build generates canonical telemetry samples (1 per API route) and asserts presence of required fields.
- Diff alert: PR adds a one-line human-readable change note in telemetry-changelog.md.

B. Production-time gates (automated monitors)
- Visibility SLO: >= 99.0% of successful requests must contain request-level trace_id and start_timestamp. If visibility drops below 98.5% for 5m, auto-open an incident and roll back the rollout wave.
- Schema compliance: > 99.5% of telemetry ingested in the last 1h must match schema_version vX.Y or acceptable backward-compatible versions. If compliance < 98.0% for 30m, disable new export feature flag and roll back.
- Telemetry bandwidth guard: Export rate from a node must remain below 2.5x of baseline for 1h. If exceeded by >2.5x and cost estimate > $20/hour/node, apply automatic sampling increase (see sampling rules) and notify on-call.
- High-cardinality protection: Unknown tag cardinality (unique tenant+route+kernel_hint pairs observed) must not grow > 20% per hour. Exceeding threshold triggers temporary cardinality-cap enforcement (truncate tag) and throttles diagnostics.

Actions associated with gate failures

- Alert and create incident if threshold breached.
- Circuit-break to conservative telemetry mode (reduced sampling, drop heavy profile payloads).
- If degradation coincides with increased error rates >0.5 p95 request latency percentiles, start automated rollback of rollout wave.

Sampling and bandwidth budget

- Default request trace sampling: 0.1% per-tenant baseline; global floor 0.01%.
- Profiling payload sampling (heavy): 1 in 10,000 by default.
- Adaptive ramping: If latency SLO violations are detected for trace-sampled requests, decrease trace sampling proportionally to reduce overhead.
- Bandwidth control policy (node-local): token-bucket that allows up to B=1000 telemetry items/min sustained with burst 2000 for short spikes. Config snippet: 

--- yaml
telemetry_export:
  node_budget_per_min: 1000
  burst_allowance: 2000
  budget_cost_weights:
    small_metric: 1
    trace: 5
    profile_blob: 50
---

Build-time validation and CI integration

1. Telemetry unit-tests: Each new PR touching runtime exports must add a test that 1) introspects the exported proto/struct, 2) serializes a canonical sample, and 3) validates against jsonschema.
2. Integration smoke: Canary job runs runtime in local harness and verifies that the exported telemetry can be ingested by the canonical ingestion lambda.
3. Preflight: As part of release build, generate a "telemetry-change report" artifact. PR must have explicit sign-off from at least one telemetry reviewer.

Runtime enforcement mechanisms

- Export agent shields: An FFI agent process buffers and enforces budget; it will drop or compress payloads if budget exceeded.
- Feature flags: New fields are behind feature flags. Feature flags are two-phase: opt-in test, shadow export, then opt-in full.
- Telemetry schema adapter: small compatibility layer that translates older schema_version to latest normalization for downstream consumers during transition.

Operational runbook (if a gate trips)

1. Pager: Receive PagerDuty alert (observability-gate).
2. Initial triage (within 5 min): Confirm gate (query ingestion).
3. If visibility SLO violation confirmed, set export_agent to conservative mode via runtime API: POST /admin/telemetry/mode -> {"mode":"conservative"}.
4. If conservative mode does not restore visibility within 10 minutes, roll back the rollout wave following "Runtime Rollback SOP" (see related_pages).
5. Post-incident: Create a telemetry incident ticket and attach canonical payload samples.

Integration checklist for changing schema

- [ ] Add fields behind FF and document intent in telemetry-changelog.md.
- [ ] Add unit and integration tests with canonical samples.
- [ ] Create rollout plan with shadow period (minimum 48 hours).
- [ ] Notify owner teams and SRE with scheduled rollout.
- [ ] Add automatic fallback that strips new fields when consumers report errors.

Examples

Example exported request metric (json-lines):
{
  "schema_version": "2026-11-v1",
  "event_type": "metric",
  "request_id": "r-6a7d7f2e",
  "model": "redwood/gptx-7b-v1",
  "tenant_id": "acme-corp",
  "route": "generate",
  "seq_len": 320,
  "tokens_generated": 64,
  "start_timestamp": "2026-11-03T18:22:10.123Z",
  "end_timestamp": "2026-11-03T18:22:10.890Z",
  "kernel_hint": "kernel-v2-mma32",
  "alloc_bytes": 12345678
}

Appendix: metric names and dashboards

- runtime.request.visibility_pct (ratio of requests with valid trace_id)
- runtime.telemetry.schema_compliance (perc matched schema_version)
- runtime.telemetry.export_rate (items/min/node)
- runtime.telemetry.payload_cost_estimate (USD/hour/node)

Ownership and rollout

- Instrumentation owners: eng-serving-runtime-observability (primary: Aisha Malik).
- SRE escalation: runtime-oncall@redwood.com.
- Rollout plan: new telemetry fields require staged rollout (dev->canary->prod waves), shadow export 48–72h, and an SLO observation period of 24h before full enable.

Related documents and references

- See Runtime Observability Self-Heal Orchestration (related_pages) for automatic rollback primitives.
- See CI telemetry-change validation job (pipeline: infra/ci/telemetry) for details on preflight checks.

Contact

For questions about schema changes or gate thresholds contact: aisha@redwood.ai or join #runtime-observability on Slack.
